<subject>Re: Arjun Commodities Ltd</subject>
<body>
I think our discussion about an incremental levy applying to suppliers of all categories was with regard to our speculation on how the "new MSP adjustment" recovery mechanism would work, not Nashik region.  I think the recovery mechanism is still speculation. There are many differing alternatives.

That's my recollection.


From: Thomas Gade on 5/28/2024 11:05 AM
To: Reyansh Krish
cc: Chakradhar Lala, Hardik D Pal, Nihal 
Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan 
Subject: RE: Arjun Commodities Ltd

I've have talked to Chakradhar.  I think I just misunderstood.
</body>

Best,
Reyansh




	Thomas Gade 5/23/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar 
Lala  cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika 
Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D 
Pal  Subject: RE: Arjun Commodities Ltd


Chakradhar, Nihal Karan, Reyansh Krish and I were on a trip with Viraj Vyas last week.  I understood from Nihal that Viraj may believe that all suppliers, including direct-contract partners, should pay the levy you mention.  Nihal?  This was encouraging from a litigation exposure standpoint because, to the extent all partners are treated alike, our direct-contract suppliers who were transitioned to spot-market procurement cannot claim to have been disadvantaged by our action. The converse is also true:  if they have to pay because they were put back on standard terms they may try to pass that cost through to us. To the extent that any increase is to reimburse NAFED for forward purchases 2/1/24-3/30/25, and those on direct contract are not required to pay this, the Procurement unit could have a substantial exposure to its partners.   Maybe we need to modify our strategy to take this into account. -----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar  
Sent: Thursday, May 23, 2024 8:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; 
Indore, Aurangabad; Stoness, Greenfield Trading; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: Arjun Commodities Ltd


Arjun's regulatory filing confirms that the soybean price support of ₹5,850/qt does not apply to independent traders.

In consultations on Arjun's potential rate adjustment for bulk buyers:
Arjun has proposed to allocate all retained inventory to smallholder partners (below 50 MT annually).  Bulk buyers would be served by NAFED (or be independent traders).  It's apparent several parties have major problems with this. It is interesting that Arjun has calculated the expected rate increase under their plan as ₹285/MT.  If bulk buyers are allocated a share of retained inventory, the increase goes up to ₹299/MT.  In the latter case, bulk buyers retain an MSP adjustment (related to forward contracts and other long-term stranded costs) that they would lose in the former case. Our involvement is to get an order 1) excluding independent traders from any rate increase (the proposed ₹285/MT) 2) excluding independent traders from any surcharge related to undercollection from the price support (an amount that is not known at this point) 3) prorating the surcharge related to undercollection if the customer
